Extract one table from a PDF page by word geometry

Source: R/pdftab-core.R
pdf_read_table.Rd

A general-purpose table reader for PDFs where pdftools::pdf_text() loses the column structure (wrapped cells, centred headers, rotated pages). It locates a table by its caption, assigns every word below the caption to a text line and then to a column, and finally groups lines into records either by vertical gaps (record = "gap") or by a column that starts every new record (record = "anchor").

Usage

pdf_read_table(
  pdf_file,
  table_id,
  page,
  header_first,
  header_span = c(0, 0),
  edges = NULL,
  centres = NULL,
  record = c("gap", "anchor"),
  anchor_col = NULL,
  stop_pat = "^(NOTE|SOURCE|Note|Source):?$",
  y_max = 650,
  x_min = -Inf,
  x_max = Inf,
  gap_factor = 1.35,
  col_names = NULL
)

Arguments

pdf_file

Path to a PDF file.

table_id

Table identifier as it appears in the caption, e.g. "2.3" or "A.6".

page

Integer page number the table (or its continuation) is on.

header_first

Regular expression matching the first word of the header line used as an anchor, e.g. "^Study$".

header_span

Integer vector c(lines_above, lines_below): how many additional lines around the anchor line belong to the header (for multi-line headers).

edges

Numeric vector of column left edges relative to the table's leftmost word. Mutually exclusive with centres.

centres

Numeric vector of absolute column centre x-coordinates. Mutually exclusive with edges.

record

Either "gap" (a new record starts after an unusually large vertical gap) or "anchor" (a new record starts on every line where column anchor_col is non-empty).

anchor_col

Integer column index used when record = "anchor".

stop_pat

Regular expression for the first word of a line that ends the table body, e.g. a "NOTE:" or "SOURCE:" line.

y_max

Discard words below this y-coordinate (footers).

x_min, x_max

Discard words outside this x-range; useful on rotated pages where running heads and page numbers sit in the margin.

gap_factor

Multiplier applied to the smallest line-to-line vertical gap to decide what counts as a "large" gap when record = "gap".

col_names

Optional character vector of output column names; defaults to the header text, cleaned with make.names().

Value

A data frame, one row per record, one column per detected column, with an attribute "header" holding the raw header text.

Details

Column boundaries must be supplied one of two ways, matching how the table is actually typeset:

  • edges: left edges of left-aligned columns, in points relative to the table's own leftmost word (so the same spec works across pages with different margins).

  • centres: absolute x centres of centred columns; each word is assigned to its nearest centre. Use pdf_suggest_edges() to measure candidate values from the page.
